ety.text: From Middle English laste, latst, syncopated variant of latest, both ultimately from Old English latost. Doublet of latest.
From Middle English lasten, from Old English lǣstan, from Proto-West Germanic *laistijan, from Proto-Germanic *laistijaną. Cognate with German leisten (“yield”).

The noun is derived from Middle English lest, leste (“shoemaker’s model shaped like a foot, last”), from Old English lǣste (“shoemaker‘s last”), from Proto-Germanic *laistiz, from *laisǭ (“track, trail”), from Proto-Indo-European *leys-eh₂-, from *leys- (“to trace; to track”). Doublet of learn and lore. The verb is derived from the noun. cognates * Dutch leest * German Leisten * Proto-Germanic *laistaz (“footprint”) * Swedish läst

From Middle English last, from Old English hlæst (“burden, load, freight”), from Proto-Germanic *hlastuz (“burden, load, freight”), from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂- (“to put, lay out”). Cognate with West Frisian lêst, Dutch last, German Last, Swedish last, Icelandic lest.

senses.d: Final, ultimate, coming after all others of its kind.
ex: Will try to fix it by myself for now: as a last resort, we can always take it to a grease monkey.
Eyes Wide Shut was the last film to be directed by Stanley Kubrick.
syn: rear, rearmost, caboose, dernier, final, terminal, ultimate, lattermost;

senses.d: Most recent, latest, last so far.
ex: The last time I saw him, he was married.
I have received your note dated the 17th last, and am responding to say that[…]

senses.d: Farthest of all from a given quality, character, or condition; most unlikely, or least preferable.
ex: He is the last person to be accused of theft.
The last person I want to meet is Helen.

senses.d: Being the only one remaining of its class.
ex: Japan is the last empire.

senses.d: Supreme; highest in degree; utmost.
ex: Contending for principles of the last importance.

senses.d: Lowest in rank or degree.
ex: Three contestants will win awards, but the last prize is just a book voucher.
In one word then, unless I could unfold the mystery, I will not wish you to consider me but as the last and lowest of mankind.

senses.d: The (one) immediately before the present.
ex: We went there last year.
I was last to go; you're next.

senses.d: Closest in the past, or closest but one if the closest was very recent; of days, sometimes thought to specifically refer to the instance closest to seven days (one week) ago, or the most recent instance before seven days (one week) ago.
ex: It's Wednesday, and the party was last Tuesday; that is, not yesterday, but eight days ago.
When you say last Monday, do you mean the Monday just gone, or the one before that?

senses.d: Most recently.
ex: When we last met, he was based in Toronto.
How long is't now since last yourself and I / Were in a mask?

senses.d: after everything else; finally
ex: As I arrived last of all, I'll go last to add the butter last.
last but not least

senses.d: To endure, continue over time.
ex: Summer seems to last longer each year.
They seem happy now, but that won't last long.

senses.d: To hold out, continue undefeated or entire.
ex: I don't know how much longer we can last without reinforcements.

senses.d: A burden; load; a cargo; freight.

ex: Now we so quietly followed our businesse, that in three moneths wee made three or foure Last of Tarre, Pitch, and Sope ashes [...].

senses.d: An old English (and Dutch) measure of the carrying capacity of a ship, equal to two tons.
ex:
1942 (1601), T D Mutch, The First Discovery of Australia, page 14,
